source_text:
Tit 2,7 Τὸ τῆς ἀδιαφορίας

ἐπὶ τοῦ νοῦ ἔλαβεν, τὸ δὲ τῆς σεμνότητος ἐπὶ τοῦ ἔργου, ἵνα μὴ μόνον ἔργου ἀπέχῃ
φθαρτοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ νοήματος.
thought_title: Incorruptibility of mind and dignity of work
orientation: Oecumenius is commenting on Paul's instruction to Titus about his own conduct, distinguishing the sphere of incorruptibility from the sphere of dignity.
pass_a_gloss: The incorruptibility he took as applying to the mind, and the dignity as applying to the work, so that he may abstain not only from corrupt work but also from corrupt thought.

lemmas.gloss: he may abstain from, keep away from

choices.term: Τὸ τῆς ἀδιαφορίας ἐπὶ τοῦ νοῦ ἔλαβεν
choices.english: The incorruptibility he took as applying to the mind
choices.why: The article with genitive marks the quality; 'took as applying to' renders the force of ἐπί with genitive of sphere.
rejected: He understood the incorruptibility to be of the mind
He took the incorruptibility upon the mind

choices.term: τὸ δὲ τῆς σεμνότητος ἐπὶ τοῦ ἔργου
choices.english: and the dignity as applying to the work
choices.why: Parallel construction with δέ marking the contrast; 'as applying to' keeps the same rendering of ἐπί.
rejected: but the dignity upon the work
and the dignity of the work

choices.term: ἵνα μὴ μόνον ἔργου ἀπέχῃ φθαρτοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ νοήματος
choices.english: so that he may abstain not only from corrupt work but also from corrupt thought
choices.why: ἵνα with subjunctive marks purpose; the adjective φθαρτοῦ is distributed to both nouns in the gloss to preserve the full sense.
rejected: so that he may abstain not only from a corrupt work but also from a thought
that he may keep away not only from corrupt work but also from corrupt thought

bible_refs.note: The lemma Tit 2,7 introduces the comment on incorruptibility and dignity, terms drawn from Paul's instruction to Titus.

pass_b_english: He understood incorruptibility as a quality of the mind, and dignity as a quality of one's work, so that a person would keep away not only from corrupt deeds but also from corrupt thoughts.

problems.why: Wait—checking: intro has 'incorruptibility of mind', fragment has same. No drift. Cancel.
Unclear 'He'—Oecumenius? Paul? Titus? Section break from prior fragment loses referent
problems.fix: Specify 'Paul understood' or 'Oecumenius understood Paul to mean'

problems.quote: He understood incorruptibility as a quality of the mind
problems.why: 'He' is ambiguous—could be Paul or Oecumenius—across the section break.

fixed: The glossary issue was cancelled by the checker; no change needed.
The ambiguity of 'He' was real; specified 'Paul' as the subject.
The second speaker issue was the same ambiguity; resolved by the same edit.
